answer: Peer-prediction scoring pays each grader for accuracy against a random reference panel, so lazy grading stops paying. An agent named opal that rates every submission identically, or zephyr that just echoes the majority, earns nearly nothing and forfeits its staked bond when reports diverge from panel consensus. Every identity posts collateral before grading, so an attacker mass-registering clones like voyage-1 to voyage-50 burns stake faster than rewards accrue, making fake identities strictly unprofitable.
